Guidance & outlook: Phase 2 of MEL is expected to commence operations next year, later than originally envisaged owing to certain challenges beyond our control with no material impact on project capex.
So, right now, we're looking at the total commissioning of both the units by Q2 of FY 27-28, around the July timeframe of next year.
Going forward, we are quite well ring -fenced against any volatilities because almost 70% of our production is already committed, either under long -term contracts or quarterly contracts.
Growth & demand: We continue to make measured progress on our next phase of growth in the energy and commercial agriculture segment.
That's helping the growth of our company in various verticals.
I think the metals business, as you know, is volume -driven rather than margin-driven.
Margins & costs: Basically, the project cost is INR400 million, out of which INR300 million is debt and INR100 is equity.
The historical cost of Nacharam land is around INR40 lakhs.
And when it comes to consolidated EBITDA, it will be between 35% to 40%.
Capex & expansion: Our Energy and Mining business delivered healthy operating performance with MEL's 300 - megawatt plant operating at a strong 89.3 PLF.
It is, however, heartening that the 100-megawatt solar power project set to be commissioned shortly would establish a new niche for Nava prompting further investments in this space.
Yes, solar plant is set to be commissioned by the end of September.
Balance sheet & cash: Our international foray also continued to provide value through dividend flows and to attain financial strength to pursue investments.
Lower coal and manufacturing costs, along with dividend income from Nava Global supported this improvement.

Subsequently, Nava Global seems to have taken over these assets and they are now being shown as profits accruing to Nava Global and Nava Global giving dividends, buying back its own shar es from Nava Limited with that money, etc.
Risks & challenges: We are cognizant of the significant challenges arising from the geopolitical and supply chain disruptions and are taking appropriate remedial actions.
Our diversified portfolio, financial strength and operational resilience should however, position us well to navigate these challenges while remaining focused on long-term value creation.

With regards to the phase 2 thermal, I also mentioned in my opening remarks, due to the current conflict that is going on in the world, we had experienced certain logistical delays with shipment of some critical material and equipment.
